sections.h2: What will the Madison County Register of Deeds do with my deed?
sections.html:
It files the signed deed in the county's permanent index, and that filing is the moment the transfer becomes visible to everyone else. The county's contact page gives 828-649-3131 for the office.

Valuation and yearly billing sit elsewhere, with Tax Administration in Marshall. The register is the keeper of paper. It checks the document, takes the fixed state fees and the seller's stamp tax, and notes the time.

Call before you travel and ask for the current counter hours, or let your closing attorney deal with the office from a distance.

Tax Administration, by contrast, posts weekday hours of 8:00am to 5:00pm at 5707 Highway 25/70, Room 25. Plan a call to each office, since a deed that is filed cleanly but left off the tax roll will keep sending the old owner a bill.

sections.h2: Why does the filing time on a Madison County deed matter?
sections.html:
Because North Carolina ranks competing claims by when each was registered. G.S. 47-18 says deeds, options, leases running beyond three years and rights of first refusal gain force against lien creditors and paying purchasers only on registration in the county where the land sits.

For a Madison County parcel, the Madison County office is therefore the only one that counts, wherever the seller lives. Excise tax on a parcel spanning two counties is paid where more of the value lies.

  • A buyer whose deed waits unfiled can lose out to a creditor who files first.
  • A new lender's deed of trust that is filed late may rank behind liens that were not meant to come first.
  • A deed filed in a neighboring county leaves the Madison County record unchanged.

This is why closings end with the deed and the loan documents going in on the same day, in the order the attorney planned.

sections.h2: What does the state charge at the Madison County counter?
sections.html:
One statute, G.S. 161-10, sets the fees for every North Carolina county alike, so Madison County has no separate schedule of its own to publish. A plain deed is $26.00 up to 15 pages, and a deed of trust is $64.00 up to 35 pages.

Two surcharges exist: $25.00 for a document in nonstandard format and $10.00 for every extra instrument bundled into one filing. Payment comes before filing.

sections.h2: Does a Madison County land split need a recorded plat first?
sections.html:
Usually yes when the split counts as a subdivision. The county's subdivision ordinance, revised June 28, 2022, says no lot shown on a required subdivision plat may be sold or transferred until the final plat has been recorded by the Register of Deeds.

The same ordinance tells the register not to file a subdivision plat that has not been approved under its rules. It also bars a building permit or a septic permit until the Planning Board has approved the final plat and the register has recorded it. Buyers of a back lot are often caught here, because a lender will not close on a parcel that cannot be permitted.

  • Combining or recombining recorded lots without adding lots is carved out, as long as the results meet the county's standards.
  • A family subdivision has its own approval, and the final plat carries a title block that says so.
  • Plats must comply with G.S. 47-30 to be suitable for recording.

The ordinance also lets an owner sign contracts to sell by reference to an approved preliminary plat before the final plat exists, though the lot itself cannot transfer until the final plat is recorded. That sequencing is worth knowing when a buyer wants to sign early. If you plan to carve a lot off a Madison County tract before selling, ask the county's subdivision administrator whether your split needs a plat, and do it before you list.

sections.h2: Who pays the Madison County deed stamp tax?
sections.html:
The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts a levy of $1.00 per $500 of price, counting any fraction of $500 as a full unit, on whoever transfers the land. The register of deeds takes the money before the deed is entered.

Half stays in county hands. Monthly remittances carry the other half to the Department of Revenue, less a 2 percent county share of it.

Read the exact figure off your settlement statement, beside the loan payoff and any tax balance. A cash purchase works the same way.

sections.h2: Can Madison County owners get an alert when a document is filed?
sections.html:
A county newsletter dated March 2022 announced one. The register of deeds offered an email notice whenever a recorded document matched a name an owner had signed up to watch. The sign-up asks for your name, your email and the names to monitor, followed by a confirmation email that may land in a junk folder.

For anyone who owns land they rarely visit, or who is settling an estate, such an alert can catch a forged deed or a stray lien the day it reaches the index. Ask the office whether the service is still running.

Electronic filing is another question for the same counter. Your closing attorney knows which vendors the office accepts.

sections.h2: How do the two Marshall offices work together after a sale?
sections.html:
Filing the deed gives the assessor the new owner. The assessor's page says that office tracks ownership changes and keeps the property maps.

  • After recording, call Tax Administration at 828-649-0734 and confirm the owner name.
  • Have the year's September 1 bill paid or credited in the closing so the lien does not follow the house.
  • Where a circuit breaker deferral exists, give the tax office 10 days to prepare deferred bills, as its page requests of attorneys.
  • Take the parcel number from the tax bill and put it on the deed paperwork.

County housing data hints at the workload: 11,874 units in 2025, with 77.5 percent owner-occupied across 2020 to 2024 (Census Bureau). Ordinary sales and family transfers dominate.

sections.h2: What should a Madison County seller have ready before closing?
sections.html:
A title agent or attorney files the paperwork. Gather these items so nothing stalls.

  • The old deed, so names can be copied exactly.
  • Payoff statements for each deed of trust on the parcel. Lenders then file cancellations, and those carry no fee.
  • The parcel number, plus a survey if the acreage is uncertain.
  • For an inherited house, estate paperwork. Small estate affidavits go to the superior court clerk, and G.S. 28A-25-1 sets the dollar limits.

A cash buyer can take a house with a tangled history, yet every link still has to be recorded properly. Running the title early gives you time to chase a missing release.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Madison County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 828-649-3131, per the county contact page. Ask about counter hours and recording options before you send anything.

faqs.q: What is the price of recording a deed in Madison County?
faqs.a: A deed of 15 pages or fewer costs $26.00, then $4.00 per added page. Mortgages and deeds of trust cost $64.00 through page 35. State law fixes both amounts.

faqs.q: Which side of the sale pays the Madison County excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller pays, at $1.00 per $500 of price, and the register takes it ahead of recording.

faqs.q: Does Madison County charge to file a mortgage release?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 sets no charge for filing a satisfaction or cancellation.

faqs.q: After recording, who updates the tax bill owner in Madison County?
faqs.a: The assessor tracks ownership changes, so confirm the new name with Tax Administration and settle the September 1 bill at closing.
